headline: Flexibility is range of motion—the ability to adapt and yield without damage
universal_truth: Rigidity breaks under stress; flexibility bends and returns; adaptability is survival
fun_facts: The most flexible trees are often the ones that survive storms—stiff trees snap
Flexibility decreases with age unless maintained—it's use it or lose it
Emotional flexibility predicts psychological wellbeing better than constant positive mood
discussion_questions: Where are you flexible and where are you rigid?
What would break if pushed versus what would bend?
How do you maintain range of motion in your thinking and behavior?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A stiff tree snaps in a storm. A flexible tree bends and springs back. Flexibility is the ability to yield without breaking—in body, mind, and life. Rigidity seems strong but often shatters under pressure.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often value strength and firmness. But flexibility is equally important. Why?

options.text: Flexibility absorbs stress that would break rigidity—by bending, you can return; by refusing to bend, you risk shattering; adaptability survives what resistance cannot
options.response: Yes. Rigid things break under enough pressure. Flexible things bend and recover. Flexibility isn't weakness—it's resilient strength. Yielding appropriately prevents breaking.

options.text: Flexibility is just useful for movement
options.response: Physically true, but the principle extends to thinking, relationships, and life approaches...

q1.title: Range of Motion
q1.script: Flexibility is range of motion—how far you can go in different directions. Wide range means many options. Narrow range means limited responses. Flexibility creates possibility.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Range of Motion"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Use It or Lose It
q2.script: Flexibility decreases without use. Joints stiffen. Thinking patterns harden. Regularly moving through your full range—physically and mentally—maintains it.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Knowing When to Bend
q3.script: Flexibility doesn't mean bending on everything. It means knowing when yielding serves you and when standing firm does. Strategic flexibility beats reflexive rigidity or compliance.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Rigidity breaks under stress; flexibility bends and returns. Adaptability is survival. Cultivate your range of motion.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 306. Tomorrow, we'll explore brain and body working together—the mind-body connection. Until then, notice where you're rigid versus flexible.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Flexibility Audit - Where Are You Rigid?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify rigidity and expand range of motion
growTrack.activity: Where are you rigid—physically, mentally, emotionally? In what positions, opinions, or habits? What would greater flexibility look like? How can you practice bending before life forces you to?
